def: A model that predicts by routing an example through a series of threshold questions on single features to a leaf holding the prediction.
A node of a tree with no further questions, holding the prediction for the examples that reach it.
A node of a tree that asks a question about one feature and sends the example to one of two children.
The first node of a tree, which asks the first question about the whole training set.
A measure of how mixed the classes (or how spread the targets) are in a node, zero for a pure node.
The probability that two examples drawn at random from a node have different labels, equal to 2p(1-p) for two classes.
The impurity measure -p log2 p - (1-p) log2 (1-p), in bits; the drop in entropy from a split is the information gain.
The parent node's impurity minus the size-weighted impurity of its children, used to score a candidate split.
A tree for a numerical target whose splits reduce the variance of the target and whose leaves predict the mean.
Classification and regression trees: the greedy, binary, recursive partitioning algorithm of Breiman, Friedman, Olshen and Stone (1984).
A procedure that makes the best choice at each step without looking ahead, as a tree does when choosing each split.
Cutting back a large tree by minimising training error plus a price per leaf, controlled by ccp_alpha.
A resample of the training rows drawn with replacement, the same size as the original.
